recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Do not reapply the exact 2018 wording or add redundant clarification because the current FHIR-39262 wording is the later published work-group clarification and directly resolves the FHIR-18645 ambiguity.
issue_request: FHIR-18645 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 vocabulary issue for FHIR-core CodeSystem asking to clarify confusing Concept Hierarchy wording: nested hierarchy was described as a single tree with one parent, immediately followed by wording about repeated parent properties and a subsumes extension.
initial_application: The seed's Jira comments state that the resolution was superseded by and applied as part of GF#19307/FHIR-19307. Git history shows c27b4eaede30c4537c55ae885110719ef3067ae0 as the actual CodeSystem source application: it removed the subsumes-extension wording, added property guidance for additional parents, and preserved CodeSystem operation equivalence for property and nested hierarchy representations.
additional_context: FHIR-19307 is already represented on the combined branch by audit commit 0c6c33bbba9384babc8a4a41d9521846e518ab66. Later Published issue FHIR-39262 and Vocabulary minutes deliberately reworded the same Concept Hierarchy paragraph to distinguish nested single-tree hierarchy from property-based polyhierarchy.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The active CodeSystem source says nested concepts alone form a single tree with one parent, properties allow polyhierarchies where concepts may have more than one parent, hierarchy represented through properties should not be mixed with nested hierarchy structure, and operations must return the same result for property and nested representations.
